title: Atoms and Molecules
seo_title: Atoms and Molecules Class 9 Science Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 3)
standard_text: Atoms and Molecules: Atoms and molecules, Law of Chemical Combination, Chemical formula of common compounds, Atomic and molecular masses.
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 9 Science worksheets for NCERT Chapter 3: laws of chemical combination, Dalton's theory, symbols, valency and chemical formulae, molecular and formula unit mass, and the mole concept. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Cross over the valencies to write a formula.
key_sub: 1 mole = 6.022 × 10²³ particles; n = mass ÷ molar mass.
body_html:
How to think about it

Mass is neither created nor destroyed in a reaction (law of conservation of mass), and a compound always has its elements in the same ratio by mass (law of constant proportions). Dalton explained both with atoms.

To write a formula, cross over the valencies of the ions (Al³⁺ and O²⁻ give Al₂O₃). Molecular mass is the sum of the atomic masses of all atoms in a molecule. One mole of anything has 6.022 × 10²³ particles, and its mass in grams equals the atomic or molecular mass in u.

Example

Formula of aluminium sulphate?

Al³⁺ and SO₄²⁻

cross over: Al₂(SO₄)₃

Answer: Al₂(SO₄)₃

Example

Moles in 36 g of water?

M = 18 g/mol

36 ÷ 18

Answer: 2 mol

Common mistakes

  • Leaving out brackets around a polyatomic ion.
  • Adding atomic masses without multiplying by the number of atoms.
  • Mixing up the mass of 1 mole with the mass of 1 molecule.

faq.q: What is the difference between a molecule and a formula unit?
faq.a: A molecule is a group of atoms bonded together (H₂O); ionic compounds such as NaCl are made of ions, so we use a formula unit.
The amount of substance that contains 6.022 × 10²³ particles (atoms, molecules or ions).

items.q: Which element has the symbol Fe?
In carbon dioxide, carbon and oxygen always combine in the mass ratio 3 : 8. What mass of oxygen combines with 1.5 g of carbon?
items.e: Law of constant proportions: 1.5 × 8 ÷ 3 = 4 g of oxygen.

items.q: Which element has the symbol P?
What is the symbol of bromine?
In hydrogen chloride, hydrogen and chlorine always combine in the mass ratio 2 : 71. What mass of chlorine combines with 8 g of hydrogen?
items.e: Law of constant proportions: 8 × 71 ÷ 2 = 284 g of chlorine.

2.65 g of sodium carbonate reacts with 9.8 g of ethanoic acid, giving 1.3 g of carbon dioxide and the rest as water and sodium ethanoate. What is the total mass of water and sodium ethanoate?
items.e: Law of conservation of mass: total mass of products = 2.65 + 9.8 = 12.5 g, so 12.5 − 1.3 = 11.2 g.

items.q: 10.6 g of sodium carbonate reacts with 6 g of ethanoic acid, giving 5.3 g of carbon dioxide and the rest as water and sodium ethanoate. What is the total mass of water and sodium ethanoate?

items.q: Which postulate of Dalton's theory explains the law of conservation of mass?
c: atoms of an element are identical
atoms are neither created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction

items.q: What is the molar mass of a substance?
c: the mass of one molecule in grams
the mass of 1 mole of it in grams
items.e: Its value equals the atomic or molecular mass in u.

items.q: What is one atomic mass unit (u)?
c: the mass of one hydrogen molecule
one-twelfth of the mass of one carbon-12 atom

items.q: Which pair has the same number of atoms?
c: 1 mole of sodium and 1 g of magnesium
1 mole of sodium and 1 mole of magnesium
1 g of sodium and 1 g of magnesium
1 g of sodium and 1 mole of magnesium

items.q: Who gave the law of constant proportions?
items.e: A compound always has its elements in the same mass ratio.

items.q: What is the formula unit mass of NaCl? (Na = 23 u, Cl = 35.5 u)
items.e: Ionic compounds have formula units, not molecules.

items.q: 2.65 g of sodium carbonate reacts with 9.8 g of ethanoic acid, giving 1.9 g of carbon dioxide and the rest as water and sodium ethanoate. What is the total mass of water and sodium ethanoate?
items.e: Law of conservation of mass: total mass of products = 2.65 + 9.8 = 12.5 g, so 12.5 − 1.9 = 10.6 g.

items.q: 5.3 g of sodium carbonate reacts with 6 g of ethanoic acid, giving 4.2 g of carbon dioxide and the rest as water and sodium ethanoate. What is the total mass of water and sodium ethanoate?
items.e: Law of conservation of mass: total mass of products = 5.3 + 6 = 11.3 g, so 11.3 − 4.2 = 7.1 g.

items.q: 10.6 g of sodium carbonate reacts with 4.9 g of ethanoic acid, giving 7.4 g of carbon dioxide and the rest as water and sodium ethanoate. What is the total mass of water and sodium ethanoate?
items.e: Law of conservation of mass: total mass of products = 10.6 + 4.9 = 15.5 g, so 15.5 − 7.4 = 8.1 g.

items.q: 4.2 g of sodium carbonate reacts with 9.8 g of ethanoic acid, giving 2.1 g of carbon dioxide and the rest as water and sodium ethanoate. What is the total mass of water and sodium ethanoate?
items.e: Law of conservation of mass: total mass of products = 4.2 + 9.8 = 14 g, so 14 − 2.1 = 11.9 g.

items.q: Which postulate of Dalton's theory explains the law of constant proportions?
c: atoms combine in a fixed whole-number ratio to form compounds
atoms of different elements differ in mass
items.e: So the mass ratio is fixed.
